positiveFindingsWorthPreserving: THE A3 DISCIPLINE IS BEING APPLIED CORRECTLY IN THE FIELD, AND I CAN SHOW BOTH SIDES OF IT FROM ONE SHIFT. Georgia and Wyoming ship the identical sentence -- 'No committed record this packet binds states a filing fee, or a fee waiver, for this route' -- and one is true and one is false. GA's compiled profile carries five money statements and every one is keyed to a different section (GCIC processing, automatic restriction, SB 288 under Sec. 35-3-37(j)(4), the GCIC report, and Sec. 42-8-66's no-fee rule), so none answers Sec. 42-8-62.1 and the denial holds. WY's carries a row keyed to 'Human-trafficking victim vacatur' by name, so the denial fails. Per fact, per route, is exactly the difference.

MISSISSIPPI APPLIES A3 INSIDE THE PACKET, TO THE PARTICIPANT. Each of its three fee rows names the neighbouring fee statute a reader would most plausibly assume applies and says why it does not: 'Section 99-19-72's fee reaches petitions under Sec. 99-19-71 and does not reach [Sec. 41-29-150 / Sec. 63-11-30 / Sec. 67-3-70] by its terms.' That is the determination's own reasoning written for a participant rather than for a verifier.

TEXAS NAMES THE WRONG NUMBER AND DISOWNS IT. 'NOW THE NUMBER TO IGNORE: $28. You may have read that an order of nondisclosure costs $28... it belongs to [the no-petition route under Sec.] 411.072(c)... Do not arrive at the clerk's window with $28.' A3 applied prospectively against the participant's own likely misreading, not just against a repairer's. Its fee waiver is shipped rather than described: the statewide Statement of Inability under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145 on the Misc. Docket No. 22-9090 form is component 4.

TEXAS REFUSES A BOX IT KNOWS THE ANSWER TO. The OCA order covers three sections and none is marked -- including the Sec. 411.0735 box that is this route's own -- because the printed sentence above them records the COURT's finding. Knowing the route and still refusing, because the box is not a statement of the route but of a judicial finding, is the harder and correct call.

MISSISSIPPI CARRIES 15 OF 15 REGISTRY STOP CONDITIONS VERBATIM, including the ones a builder would be tempted to soften ('Every DUI. All DUI packets carry mandatory attorney review before filing'), and adds the truest sentence in these six: obtaining the district attorney's approval as to form is the practical gate on the entire Mississippi product, it is a negotiation and not a filing, and a declining or silent prosecutor is an attorney handoff.

MISSISSIPPI STATES A VENUE TRAP RATHER THAN A VENUE. The DUI route says to file in the CIRCUIT COURT of the county of conviction even where the conviction was entered in a municipal or justice court, because the Attorney General has opined that a municipal court judge is not authorized to expunge a DUI conviction. That is the difference between a destination stated and a destination gestured at.

NORTH DAKOTA'S FIRST QUESTION IS WHETHER THE PARTICIPANT NEEDS TO FILE AT ALL. Before anything else it says that if the order of nonconviction was entered on or after 1 August 2025 they should do nothing, because the court closes the record automatically after 61 days. A packet that opens by telling some of its readers to put it down is doing the obligation's real work.

NORTH DAKOTA REFUSES A BLANK ON THE FORM'S OWN AUTHORITY. The judicial district is left empty and the reason is quoted from the printed page the participant is holding: 'If you don't know the Judicial District, you may leave that space blank.' Its place-of-signing state and country blanks carry the strongest reasoning I read: a shared binder had written the participant's state of RESIDENCE into the place-of-signing state and would have printed 'XX' as a country, so both were classified unwritable by role.

MASSACHUSETTS TELLS THE PARTICIPANT NOT TO SERVE ANYONE, AND SAYS WHY, FROM THEIR OWN PAPER. 'YOU DO NOT SERVE THE DISTRICT ATTORNEY... if upon review of your Petition it is determined that you meet all of the criteria, THAT OFFICE will then notify the District Attorney's Office.' Inventing a service obligation would have contradicted a document in the participant's hand, and the build says so.

MASSACHUSETTS GIVES REASONS FOR BLANKS INSTEAD OF LEAVING THEM BARE. Race, ethnicity, gender and the Social Security number are each stated to be blank because the platform does not collect or hold them and will not guess. A packet that silently left them would be a smaller defect than one that guessed; one that says why is better than either.

WYOMING STATES ITS STOPPING POINT AS A TRAUMA BOUNDARY, NOT ONLY AS AN ELIGIBILITY BOUNDARY. Its first stop condition is the compiled profile's own handling rule, quoted: ask only what is necessary, then route to manual/legal review, do not require graphic details. No page in the packet asks for an account of what was done to the participant, and C3-C6 are blank on the delivered paper. It is the only one of the six whose restraint is about the participant rather than about the record.

GEORGIA PUBLISHES A CONFLICT IN THE RECORD RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT QUIETLY. It states the destination as not recorded and says why -- the census records a held route-presentation conflict for this route and rejects the crosswalk edge -- instead of reading a court out of a compiled presentation the repository itself calls conflated.

THE BLIND SPOT IS REAL AND THE PACKETS SURVIVE IT. All three of my families on UNCLASSIFIED_BLANKS_BLIND_SPOT.json do carry a caption court blank that no counter can see. On all three the delivered page labels it in a parenthetical directly beneath the dot run, and the instructions name the same court. The counter is blind; the packet is not.
questionsRaisedNotDecided: VA10-Q1 (WY, ROUTE_IDENTITY). The bound Wyoming profile names this route's instrument 'Motion to Vacate Conviction under W.S. 6-2-708' and calls the route 'a motion route, not a standard expungement filing-fee route'. The delivered document is captioned PETITION. Whether a clerk handed a Petition on a motion route would open a new civil action -- which is where the standard expungement fee attaches, and so is the practical point of the profile's own fee row -- is a Wyoming practice question. Scored PASS because the route, statute and relief are unambiguous; the naming is referred.

VA10-Q2 (ND, CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP). The boundary fixture refuses 'City State Zip Code' at the 6pt floor reporting requiredWidthAtMin 179.0 against a widget width of 181.35 -- by its own two numbers the value fits. A padding inset the report does not surface is the likely explanation. It errs toward asking the participant, which is safe, so it is not scored as a defect; but a refusal whose stated arithmetic does not support it is either a reporting gap or a threshold nobody has written down.

VA10-Q3 (scope of A4's extension). SELF_HELP_STOP was scored against the committed track registry's selfHelpStopConditions for each family's trackId, treating an absent condition as a failure. DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A4 extends the ask-the-repository-first test to REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, FILING_DESTINATION, SERVICE and FEE_AND_WAIVER and does not name SELF_HELP_STOP. I read the extension as reaching it, because a registry's selfHelpStopConditions ARE the repository's statement of where a track's self-help stops, and omitting one is the failure mode A4 describes. If Captain reads that list as exhaustive, the MA and TX SELF_HELP_STOP failures should be re-read against the narrower rule -- not waived, because both are omissions of facts the repository establishes, but possibly re-scored onto another obligation.
